name: Club
effect: A simple bludgeon of hardwood, often little more than a heavy cudgel.

name: Dagger
effect: A short double-edged blade suited to close fighting, utility work, and concealment.

name: Sword
effect: A one-handed fighting sword of the sort carried by knights, guards, and professional soldiers.

name: Longsword
effect: A longer, heavier sword designed for powerful cuts and thrusts while retaining enough balance for defense.

name: Axe
effect: A sturdy one-handed axe equally familiar as a tool and battlefield weapon.

name: Mace
effect: A heavy-headed bludgeon designed to crush through armor and bone.

name: Warhammer
effect: A compact military hammer built to concentrate force against armored opponents.

name: Light Spear
effect: A light thrusting spear balanced well enough to be cast at nearby foes.

name: Spear
effect: A stout two-handed spear used to hold ground against infantry and charging enemies.

name: Greatsword
effect: A massive two-handed sword requiring skill and training to wield effectively.

name: Greataxe
effect: A heavy two-handed axe capable of inflicting devastating wounds.

name: Maul
effect: An enormous two-handed hammer whose crushing blows are especially dangerous to armored foes.

name: Polearm
effect: A long-shafted battlefield weapon combining reach with a cutting or thrusting head.

name: Pike
effect: A very long infantry spear intended for formation fighting. Cannot be used to attack targets at Engaged range.

name: Lance
effect: A heavy cavalry spear intended for the charge. Normally requires two hands. May be used one-handed while mounted. A mounted Charge with a lance gains Pierce 2.

name: Staff
effect: A long hardwood staff used as both a walking implement and defensive weapon.

name: Shield
effect: A sturdy handheld shield used to ward off melee blows and missiles.

name: Dart
effect: A small weighted throwing weapon intended for short-ranged harassment.

name: Throwing Knife
effect: A compact knife balanced specifically for throwing.

name: Sling
effect: A simple leather or woven sling capable of hurling stones with surprising force.

name: Bow
effect: A conventional hunting and war bow common throughout much of Westeros.

name: Longbow
effect: A powerful long-limbed bow requiring considerable strength and practice to use effectively.

name: Light Crossbow
effect: A compact mechanical bow that is easier to aim than a hand bow but slower to reload.

name: Heavy Crossbow
effect: A powerful crossbow built with a heavy prod and spanning mechanism, capable of defeating substantial armor.
